title: Burst Balloons
description: Calculate maximum coins by bursting balloons with boundary values of 1.
pseudocode:
1. Add 1s to both ends of nums
2. Initialize dp table of size (n+2)x(n+2)
3. For length from 1 to n:
4.   For left from 1 to n - length + 1:
5.     right = left + length - 1
6.     For i from left to right:
7.       dp[left][right] = max(dp[left][right], dp[left][i-1] + arr[left-1]*arr[i]*arr[right+1] + dp[i+1][right])

steps.note: Starting DP for length 1 (bursting single balloons)
Calculate larger ranges, eventually filling dp[1][4]
Optimal value calculated for full range [1, 4] is 167

fullDescription:
You are given n balloons, indexed from 0 to n - 1. Each balloon is painted with a number on it represented by an array nums. You are asked to burst all the balloons.

If you burst the ith balloon, you will get nums[i - 1] * nums[i] * nums[i + 1] coins. If i - 1 or i + 1 goes out of bounds of the array, then treat it as if there is a balloon with a 1 painted on it.

Return the maximum coins you can collect by bursting the balloons wisely.

 

Example 1:

Input: nums = [3,1,5,8]
Output: 167
Explanation:
nums = [3,1,5,8] --> [3,5,8] --> [3,8] --> [8] --> []
coins =  3*1*5    +   3*5*8   +  1*3*8  + 1*8*1 = 167

Example 2:

Input: nums = [1,5]
Output: 10

 

Constraints:

  • n == nums.length
  • 1 <= n <= 300
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 100
